submitted.rationale: All three measured EQEs are about zero, so the library appears essentially inactive at 2.4 eV. The stable Sb–Y–O phases are predicted to have gaps above 2.4 eV: YSbO4 about 3.0 eV, Y3Sb5O12 3.4 eV, Y3SbO7 3.6 eV. Index 28, the most Sb-rich composition, gave the least negative value (-0.00035%). It was targeted because the Sb6O13 phase is predicted to have a gap of about 2.05 eV.

rejected.reason: Targets YSbO4 (on the hull, gap about 2.97 eV); measured EQE -0.00041%
Targets Y3SbO7 (on the hull, gap about 3.6 eV); measured EQE -0.00079%
The small predicted gaps belong to off-hull structures (MACE 0.07–0.12 eV/atom above hull), so they are unlikely to form

consultations.verdict: Support: YSbO4 (Sb 0.5) is on the MACE hull with HSE gap ~2.97 eV, the lowest gap among stable ternaries (Y3SbO7 3.6, Y3Sb5O12 3.4), closest to 2.4 eV illumination. Index 23 (Sb 0.52) targets it.

Support: the mixed-valence Sb6O13 phase is predicted to have an HSE gap of about 2.05 eV, below 2.4 eV, so it can absorb the light. The most Sb-rich composition (index 28) is the most likely to contain Sb-oxide phases. YSbO4 at index 23 gave about zero EQE.

Uninformative to weakly against. Y3SbO7 is on the hull, but its predicted gap is about 3.6 eV, above 2.4 eV. Both measurements on the Sb-rich side gave about zero, so the Y-rich side is the only unexplored region. Index 14 (Sb 0.236) targets the stable Y3SbO7 phase.
